clue.text: Asian national having stake in parts of East

indicators.note: the stake sits in the middle of the compass parts, so 'in' signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: NE and SE, north-east and south-east, are compass points containing E
a pale is a pointed wooden stake, as in a paling fence

explanation.surface: A traveller from Asia owns a share in some eastern regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' looks like a financial share, but it is a fence post, and 'parts of East' are two compass points that both contain E.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Nepal, a country in South Asia, is a Nepalese.

clue.text: Venue for late shows near West End hit

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter

parts.note: to club is to hit with a stick

explanation.surface: A theatre near London's West End scores a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End', London's theatre district, is split: 'End' takes the last letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-night entertainment venue with music, dancing and cabaret shows.

clue.text: Dedicated aide bringing in an expert that's the ultimate solver

indicators.note: the aide takes the other pieces into the middle, so they sit inside

parts.note: PA, a personal assistant, is devoted to one person's needs
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A loyal assistant calls in a specialist who can fix anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all or universal remedy is the final answer to every problem.

clue.text: Instructive experience loser has got in 25

definitions.meaning: something that teaches you, a learning experience
in strip poker the loser has fewer clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25 across, strip poker.
explanation.definitionFit: An experience that teaches is one of these; split in two it says what a losing strip poker player wears.

clue.text: Lacking success in sport, not yet ready to play?

definitions.meaning: having failed to score any points or goals
jokingly, a musician without the written music cannot yet perform

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests sport again, but the second sense is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A match finishing with no goals; or playfully, missing the sheet music needed to perform.

clue.text: King Edward, for example, as lawgiver?

definitions.meaning: King Edward is a variety of potato
... law (whatever can go wrong will) is named after him, making him a jocular lawgiver

explanation.walkthrough: King Edward reads as a monarch, but it is a potato variety well known in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a potato, of which King Edward is a British variety; also the man behind the famous law of things going wrong.

clue.text: North American policeman set free after short time

indicators.note: the freeing piece comes after the time piece in the answer

parts.note: mo is short for moment
to untie is to release from bonds

explanation.surface: A cop releases a suspect after a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is known by this informal name.

clue.text: Hunting dog or rabid terrier biting vet endlessly

indicators.note: the mad terrier bites, holding the trimmed vet between its jaws
a rabid animal is mad, so the word is jumbled into a new arrangement
the word vet loses its final letter

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor, taken as written
the final letter of vet, which 'endlessly' drops; the word 'or' is only a link

explanation.surface: A mad terrier attacks the veterinarian, a hazard of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting' looks like the dog's attack, but it means holding: the jumbled terrier (RETRIER) clamps vet, trimmed to VE, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed trained to fetch shot game, used in hunting.

clue.text: Nonconformist, at this point, leading movement out of control

indicators.note: the place piece comes first, ahead of the other

parts.note: here means in this place
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A rebel heads a protest movement that has gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a political cause, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose beliefs depart from accepted doctrine, a dissenter.

clue.text: Machine's original piece

parts.note: a piece is slang for a firearm, and the weapon that came first, before the 'machine' was put in front of it, is the plain firearm

explanation.surface: Talk of the first component of some machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a component, but it is slang for a firearm; the machine-gun began as a plain one.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon is called a piece in slang, and the machine variety was built from that basic firearm.

clue.text: Athlete photographed in front of golf club

indicators.note: the first piece stands ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: shot is a past participle meaning photographed or filmed
a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A sportsman poses for a picture outside a golf clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' suggests a clubhouse, but it is the stick used on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in the field event of throwing a heavy ball is a kind of athlete.

clue.text: Idle a short time before part of test

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'
an over is a set of six balls in cricket, part of a Test match

explanation.surface: Someone lazes briefly before sitting part of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' looks like an exam, but it is a Test match in cricket, divided into overs.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that runs slowly while disengaged is idling, which the British also describe with this phrase.

clue.text: Hit with try that's converted — a score and a half

indicators.note: a rugby try that is converted is turned into something more, so these letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rugby report: a try is converted, adding points to the tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' borrows rugby, where a try is converted for extra points.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and half a score is ten, so together they make the number between twenty-nine and thirty-one.

clue.text: Bound, as 1984 was

definitions.meaning: to bound is to jump or spring
1984 was divisible by four, so it had a 29th of February

explanation.walkthrough: 1984 suggests the Orwell novel, but it is simply a year with 366 days.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump or spring, and the kind of year with an extra day in February, which 1984 was.

clue.text: Smashed plates in smithereens, visibly embarrassed

indicators.note: broken into tiny bits, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: red-faced with shame

explanation.surface: Someone who has broken the crockery blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' looks like breakage, but it is the definition: drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for very drunk, like hammered or wasted.

clue.text: China set difficult problem with corruption

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzling question, a brain-teaser
vice is moral corruption or depravity

explanation.surface: Beijing poses a hard question about graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching collection of porcelain cups, saucers and pot for serving the afternoon brew.

clue.text: A king in bowler that's seen on yacht

indicators.note: the article and monarch go inside the bowler

parts.note: a spinner is a slow bowler in cricket
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch in a bowler hat is spotted on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests a hat, but it is a cricket spin bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, billowing triangular sail flown on a racing boat.

clue.text: Pressure absorbed by one-time writer's helper who removes blocks?

indicators.note: the pressure is soaked up inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former
an editor helps an author shape a text

explanation.surface: A former editor feels the strain of a writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocks' suggests writer's block, but means obstacles in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speeds up progress by clearing obstacles out of the way.

clue.text: Crazy family that creates pedestrian problem

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad or crazy
kin means relatives or family

explanation.surface: A mad household causes trouble for people on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' suggests dullness, but here it means someone walking, who may slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit peel dropped on the pavement is the classic slapstick hazard for anyone walking along.

clue.text: Beasts of burden crossing beyond deep chasms

explanation.surface: Pack animals traverse the land past steep ravines.

clue.text: A suggestion a learner finally rejected is pertinent

indicators.note: the ending of the suggestion is thrown out

parts.note: a proposal is a suggestion
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A trainee's idea is turned down in the end, though it was relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant or to the point, from the French for 'to the purpose'.

clue.text: What's behind question about your political status spelled out in speech?

parts.note: asking 'Are you MP?', whether you are a Member of Parliament

explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you' said aloud sounds like the letters R and U, and MP is a Member of Parliament.

clue.text: Leaders eliminated from cup — it might become tense

clue.text: Clear support for position that's deteriorating

explanation.surface: Plain backing for a political stance that is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotting and decaying, going bad.

clue.text: World as place of opportunity as one got out of bed?

definitions.meaning: from the saying 'the world is your ...', a world full of chances
this shellfish is harvested from beds on the sea floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Got out of bed' suggests waking up, but it is a shellfish bed.

clue.text: Informally dressed? That's not right

explanation.definitionFit: Inappropriate or ill-matched, and playfully, wearing no formal jacket and trousers.

clue.text: Game an unlucky player can barely finish

clue.text: A team's utterances supposedly not heard by other players

clue.text: Dart and rope involved in hunting animal
